translations.text: It is shameful how much my thoughts stray away from me. I fear the danger this brings on the day of everlasting Judgement.
During the psalms my thought wanders on a path that is not right. It runs about, it causes disturbance, it misbehaves before the eyes of great God.
Through lively assemblies, through crowds of foolish women, through woods, through cities: it is swifter than the wind.
One time it goes along handsome paths, and another time along ugly ones (that is no lie).
Without a boat, with its crooked step, it crosses every sea. Swiftly it leaps in a single leap from earth to heaven.
It runs near and far, and its running is not very wise. After courses of great folly it comes back to its own home.
Though one tries to bind it or to put fetters on its foot, it is not constant, and it does not think to keep still.
Neither blade nor the sound of a whip-lash subdues it firmly. It is as slippery as an eel's tail as it slips out of my grasp.
Neither lock, nor strongly vaulted prison, nor any fetter at all, neither fort, nor sea, nor bleak stronghold holds it back from its course.
O dear, truly chaste Christ, to whom every eye is clear, may the grace of the sevenfold Spirit come to keep it and restrain it.
Rule this heart of mine, O swift God of the elements, so that you may be my love and so that I may do your will.
May I reach you, O Christ, my perfect companion, and may we be together. You are not unsteady or inconstant; you are not like me.
